_comment: Shared fixtures for the golden parity test between scripts/risk/formulas.py and client/src/lib/simulatorFormulas.ts. See tests/test_golden_hex_risk_parity.py for how these are used.

tier1_vectors._comment: Hex-independent numeric test vectors for the pure formula functions -- both engines MUST agree on these to floating-point precision (same math, same inputs, no legitimate reason to diverge). This is the real regression gate: run before any change to formulas.py or simulatorFormulas.ts.
tier1_vectors._flood_sensitivity_note: slope=35 and slope=50 rows are the Bug-3 clamp case (slope>30, must NOT go negative) -- this is exactly the pattern that silently drifted between formulas.py and simulatorFormulas.ts earlier this session before both were fixed.
tier1_vectors._compute_risk_note: hazard=10 and hazard=12 rows exercise the AC-dampening floor (max(0.2, 1-H/12)) -- Bug 5's docstring-vs-code mismatch was here.

tier2_scenario._comment: Shared 'severe day' weather, applied identically to every hex on both sides for the Tier-2 hex-level comparison. rainfall=50mm and tmax=44C/hot_days=3 match hex_risk.py's own hardcoded reference values for pluvial_flood_score/heatwave_score (see hex_risk.py compute_hex_risk, the flood_sev and heat_sev lines) -- chosen so the comparison isolates real-input resolution (slope/water-distance/sand%/exposure/AC), not different weather assumptions. rh_pct is NOT fixed here -- it's computed per-hex in the Python harness from hex_risk.py's own rh_proxy formula and written into hexes_with_scenario.json so both sides use the identical value.
